name: Web app manifest members by browser
plain: Most manifest settings that make an installed web app feel native work only in Chromium browsers.
meaning: Safari 17 and iOS cover display, id, scope, icons and theme color. Firefox on computers covers none of the install surface. Desktop Chromium alone gets file handlers, protocol handlers, launch handler, note taking and tabbed mode.

web.api: manifest.webmanifest members (display, display_override, share_target, shortcuts, file_handlers, protocol_handlers, launch_handler, scope_extensions, categories, screenshots)

edge.note: Same as Chrome plus widgets and sidebar members

safari.note: display, id, scope, icons, theme_color, shortcuts (17.4 macOS), categories (17.4)

ios_safari.note: display, id, scope, icons and theme_color; icons since 15.4 but apple-touch-icon still takes priority

data.metric: Most manifest settings that make an installed web app feel native work only in Chromium browsers.

fields.name: file_handlers, protocol_handlers, launch_handler, note_taking, scope_extensions, tabbed, window-controls-overlay

limits.headline: Which install features a site gets depends mostly on the browser engine
limits.user_action: None, the page reads it silently
can: Give a Chromium install its own window, icon, shortcuts and share target
Register as a file or link handler on desktop Chromium
Set name, icon and colors almost everywhere except Firefox on computers
cannot: Reach the desktop only members from Safari, Firefox or a phone
Count on lang, dir or iarc_rating_id, which no browser acts on
Install anything without your say so
limits.differs: Android Chrome keeps share_target, shortcuts and screenshots. Desktop Chromium keeps the rest. Safari and iPhone keep the basics. Firefox desktop keeps none.

story.what_it_is: The manifest is a settings file for an installed site. Which settings count depends on the browser.

marketing.name: Web app manifest reference
marketing.pitch: Lists every manifest member and which browsers use it.

story.for_you: The same site can look like a real app in one browser and like a plain tab in another. Nothing is asked of you.
story.for_makers: Makers feature detect and treat the extra members as progressive enhancement.

use_cases.example: An editor registers as the handler for its own file type on desktop Chrome.
A player adds jump list shortcuts to its installed icon.

risks: Can look like a real app
Tracking parameters in start_url can reveal launches
story.android_note: Android Chrome adds share target, shortcuts and screenshots.
story.ios_note: iOS keeps display, id, scope, icons and theme color. Everything else is ignored.

technical_bounds: Desktop only members: file_handlers, protocol_handlers, launch_handler, note_taking, scope_extensions, tabbed, window-controls-overlay
lang, dir and iarc_rating_id have no consumer in any browser
handle_links and tab_strip are low confidence
